principal.definition: Climactic Mazama bulk airborne fallout, including co-ignimbrite ash. Both endpoints of an eligible complete-bed range enter as one interval event. Primary-coded Buckland observations with a local quantity enter by default, subject to documented site exceptions.

principal_limits.derivation: Young explicitly gives <5 cm for distal site 24. Buckland lists 5 cm. Preserve the strict source reading on the equivalent scale.
principal_limits.qualifications: Use Young’s published upper equivalent if the original target mass is represented by the site estimate and original bulk density is at least 700 kg/m³. Lower density or net export can violate this ceiling. Other additive phases or imported material can inflate the ceiling.

principal_limits.derivation: The 5 cm tephra V is independently measured and compositionally distinguished from tephra VI. The investigators specifically discuss rapid settling and possible subaqueous flow in connection with its unusual magnetic direction. The logged deposit may exceed local fallout.
principal_limits.qualifications: Conditional on complete local retention within this package and sufficient thickness after compaction. Extra catchment or lake sediment can enlarge the package. Erosion, compaction, or noncapture can invalidate the ceiling.

principal_limits.derivation: Table S2 places ash at 102 cm between wood samples at 75.5 and 130 cm. The enclosing 54.5 cm is a gross ceiling under full capture. The older age of reworked wood at 130 cm invalidates that radiocarbon tie for the age model; its physical depth is documented. S1’s 1 cm is retained separately as a compilation reading.
principal_limits.qualifications: Conditional on complete local retention within this package and sufficient thickness after compaction. Extra catchment or lake sediment can enlarge the package. Erosion, compaction, or noncapture can invalidate the ceiling.

principal_limits.derivation: The compiler quotes a 6 cm bed. The original authors report approximately 50 kg/m² of fall and later a 2–8 cm tephra facies range. The thickness and mass imply approximately 833 kg/m³ if they correspond. Admit 6 cm as a conditional ceiling on original local thickness at the composite.
principal_limits.qualifications: Conditional upper endpoint. At least the original local bulk thickness must be represented within the recovered interval. Catchment input can enlarge the package. Net export, erosion, compaction or missing core can invalidate the ceiling. The precise 6 cm remains a compiled site reading. The independent article confirms the airfall facies and approximate mass. The mass alone requires an original bulk density for a thickness conversion.

principal_limits.derivation: Long et al. (2011) measured a distinct 50 cm package at 4.84–5.34 m in the Tumalo core and assigned it by chronology. Local sediment focusing and retention were not calibrated. The original 50 cm observation is preserved.

principal_limits.derivation: Whitlock et al. (2011), core collection and chronology, sampled a 3.00 m long core and chemically identified Mazama. S1 places the horizon inside at 2.47 m. The whole recovered core gives an outer 300 cm ceiling.
principal_limits.qualifications: A broad container bound assumes complete local capture and negligible net thinning. The 60 cm short core and 247 cm burial depth are separate quantities.

principal_limits.derivation: McKay (2012), §3.4.3.4 and Fig. 3.8. A 14 cm silicic bed from 267–281 cm was attributed by grain size and stratigraphy. Other mafic layers are distinct. Sediment delivery at this Round Lake, Oregon, is uncalibrated.
principal_limits.qualifications: Conditional on complete local retention within this package and sufficient thickness after compaction. Extra catchment or lake sediment can enlarge the package. Erosion, compaction, or noncapture can invalidate the ceiling.

principal_limits.derivation: Both original studies place Carp Ash-3 at 364–368 cm. The 4 cm thickness is a preserved-bed reading. S1 lists 2 cm. The fit uses a 4 cm ceiling and one likelihood across the source core labels.
principal_limits.qualifications: Conditional local ceiling assumes the original fall was fully retained in this interval and compaction, erosion or noncapture did not make the preserved package thinner than the original local fall. Focusing or added sediment can enlarge it. The early-Holocene drying history makes loss possible.

principal_limits.derivation: S1 explicitly reports overthickening of the 60 cm Moscow bed. Lidstrom reconstructs approximately 30 cm of original ash without documenting a site-specific correction factor.
principal_limits.qualifications: The entire measured package bounds local fall only under full retention. The 30 cm reconstruction remains a source estimate.

principal_limits.derivation: The Buckland extraction gives both contacts, 7.21–7.27 m, and the independent dating crosswalk brackets Mazama at Davis Lake. principal_limits.derivation: Mehringer’s Fig. 15 shows a distinct Mazama band near 7.7–8.1 m in a fen with recurrent fire-related slopewash. On the 1120-pixel print the 6.5 and 10.5 m ticks are at y=171 and 686; the outside edges at 324 and 378 imply ≤42 cm after outward rounding. The original pollen archive samples 770 and 810.5 cm on either side, and the 771 cm age tie corroborates the horizon. The compiler’s 39 cm is compatible with the recovered bed; original dry-land fallout may have been substantially thinner.
principal_limits.qualifications: Conditional on complete local retention within this package and sufficient thickness after compaction. Extra catchment or lake sediment can enlarge the package. Erosion, compaction, or noncapture can invalidate the ceiling.

principal_limits.derivation: Leopold et al. (1982) report an 11 m core. Gyttja samples QL-1513 and QL-1514 are reported above and below Mazama in the published age crosswalk. Their depths do not define a measured bed. Use the recovered core length as the outer enclosure.

principal_limits.qualifications: Original local climactic fallout, conditional on the author primary-fall estimate and treating target as contained in their Mazama package. Published1986, not1996 as some repository metadata states. Most mapped ash-rich sediments contain less than10% unmixed primary ash; 25 cm mixed deposit is excluded. Do not multiply this percentage into a thickness. Quantitative basis of original estimate is not fully documented; test isolated omission and a weaker10 cm upper ceiling. If two falls include a precursor, an upper bound on their nonnegative sum also bounds the climactic share. Exact decimal typography pending.

principal_limits.derivation: The two identified non-target stratigraphic levels in B100NC-1 enclose at most 151.25 − 137.5 = 13.75 cm. Uses the primary Table 2 bracket without assuming which bed contact 147.5 cm represents.

principal_limits.derivation: The May 1985 core places the entire identified ash interval between 282 and 345 cm. Later input is documented. Under full primary capture, the 63 cm preserved total is a ceiling on its primary share.

principal_limits.derivation: The field guide describes a mature outwash soil and lag buried by approximately 50 cm of Mazama ash. A climactic portion of the retained package cannot exceed its total under the stated preservation assumptions.

principal_limits.derivation: Four cm of glass-rich sediment is a conditional ceiling if this horizon captured the complete local signal and redeposition or background sediment added thickness.

principal_limits.derivation: Entire visible horizon lies between two independently dated plant macrofossil levels. 440 − 320.5 = 119.5 cm.

Several hundred mg of each tephra were prepared for analysis. Processing yield, ash purity and focusing prevent calibration of a precise original bulk thickness from mounted material.

principal_limits.derivation: The author physically collected contiguous early and late Holocene charcoal intervals. Their inner ends at 180 and 405 cm enclose the 395 cm tephra marker and give a gross ≤225 cm section. The Neotoma raw charcoal series starts its older block at 405.5 cm. The chronology program removed ash thickness; its anchor width and Fig. 2 line give no physical bed measurement.

added_observation.locality: Bolan Lake, Oregon, central long core

added_observation.age_basis: Table 2 uses the published eruption age as a stratigraphic tie. The 2008 reanalysis uses the same core and horizon.
added_observation.citation: Briles, C. E., Whitlock, C. and Bartlein, P. J. (2005), Postglacial vegetation, fire, and climate history of the Siskiyou Mountains, Oregon, USA, Quaternary Research 64(1), 44–56.
added_observation.locator: Site description and Methods p. 45, Chronology p. 47, Table 2 p. 48
added_observation.decision: Thickness measured in one central lake core. The authors assign 7627 cal yr BP as an eruption-age tie and report no independent glass match or correction for focusing, compaction or redistribution. Use the preserved discrete bed as the local fallout measurement.
